The observed proportional relationship between fundamental frequency f₁ and the inverse square of the circumference is also similar to the relationship between frequency and length of a stiff straight bar.

Rossing also notes that for vibrations in a stiff bar the frequency depends on L² rather than L as in a vibrating string and the modes of frequency go as the square of odd integers. The modes sequence begins with M=3.0112 and then continues with integer values 5, 7, 9… This does not correspond exactly with our results in which the mode sequences begin with n = 1. Measurements of greater precision might shed more light on the analysis.

Future work might involve actual measurements of wave speeds for transverse wave trains traveling around the hoop. Such direct observations of wave velocities would require ultra high speed imaging that might challenge the present technology.
